datasets.name: bucky_32
datasets.decision: Distinct catalog entry; no established duplicate in the OME-Zarr collection.
datasets.description: C60 Buckminsterfullerene volume distributed by AVS (32^3).
source_notes: Source: AVS International Center. Cignoni, Montani, Puppo and Scopigno, Optimal Isosurface Extraction from Irregular Volume Data (1996), acknowledge Bucky as a 32x32x32 subsampling of a regular rectilinear dataset supplied by AVS. Original resolution, original model author and calculation method are not specified. https://iris.cnr.it/retrieve/c45d5a5c-0f9d-41c0-b554-fa5949929432/prod_408374-doc_143296.pdf

Attribution correction: user comparison found this AVS 32^3 dataset different from Oliver Kreylos' 64^3 and 128^3 datasets. The earlier assignment to his Gaussian model is withdrawn; a shared origin or use of that construction method is not established. The Volume Library's word 'Simulation' does not by itself establish a physical electron-density computation.
datasets.credits: AVS, USA http://www.avs.com
datasets.parameters: Simulation of the electron density of a Buckminster-Fullerene
datasets.size_basis: Coarse full-grid size estimate based on the known C60 cage diameter (about 0.71 nm) and outer molecular diameter (about 1 nm). Exact atom positions, field boundary and padding are not calibrated; this is not an acquisition measurement. Diameter convention reference: https://doi.org/10.1021/nl503388f . Supersedes the arbitrary 1 m display scale.

datasets.name: bunny
datasets.decision: Decoded voxel payload is SHA-512 identical to the Open SciVis raw source (bunny); prefer the earlier Volume Library distribution.
datasets.credits: Terry Yoo High Performance Computing and Communications, National Library of Medicine, USA mailto:yoo@nlm.nih.gov
datasets.comments: This is a CT scan of the terracotta Stanford Bunny. Three hundred sixty-one files comprise the bunny. The scale of the voxel data is 0.337891 mm x 0.337891 mm x 0.5mm in the x-, y-, and z- dimensions respectively. The greyscale units are Hounsfield units, denoting electron-density of the subject. The data is raw 512x512 slices, unsigned, 12 bit data stored as 16bit (2-byte) pixels. The scan was completed 28 January 2000. Many many thanks to Geoff Rubin who helped me to scan the data, Sandy Napel who coordinated the scan and helped to process the data, and Marc Levoy who graciously provided the subject. Geoff and Sandy are with Stanford Radiology, and Marc is with Stanford Computer Science. Dataset contact info: Terry S. Yoo High Performance Computing and Communications yoo@nlm.nih.gov National Library of Medicine National Institutes of Health
datasets.size_basis: 512 X voxels * 0.337891 mm = 0.173000192 m. Original CT README explicitly specifies mm; not the laser-scanned mesh. https://graphics.stanford.edu/data/voldata/bunny-README

datasets.decision: Decoded voxel payload is SHA-512 identical to the Open SciVis raw source (frog); prefer the earlier Volume Library distribution.

datasets.comments: This is the second frog used in the Whole Frog Project. Three sets of data were produced with the MRI scans. frog2ci.hips seemed to be the best, and only this set of data was processed using HIPS filters to balance the contrast on the images. This same frog was later sliced and a better data set is produced that showed more detail of the frog. frog2ci.hips -- is a spin echo data set with 50 slices, inplane resolution of 0.5mm, slice thickness and separation of 1.0mm, TE = 33ms. The individual slices 2-45 are in the tiff directory. For information about the HIPS file format see http://www-itg.lbl.gov/ITG.hm.pg.docs/image-proc/CCS-ECL/README.txt This data is copyrighted by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
datasets.size_basis: Small frog with scan margin.

datasets.comments: BrainWeb: Simulated Brain Database As the interest in the computer-aided, quantitative analysis of medical image data is growing, the need for the validation of such techniques is also increasing. Unfortunately, there exists no `ground truth' or gold standard for the analysis of in vivo acquired data. The BrainWeb pages provide a solution to the validation problem, in the form of a Simulated Brain Database (SBD). The SBD contains a set of realistic MRI data volumes produced by an MRI simulator. These data can be used by the neuroimaging community to evaluate the performance of various image analysis methods in a setting where the truth is known. PD = MRI Proton Density T1 = MRI T1 measurement T2 = MRI T2 measurement
datasets.size_basis: Approximate anatomical or object scale; no physical calibration established.
